documents.title: IFRS 9 Mortgages Reference Data Set documentation

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This document is the reference data set (RDS) documentation of the IFRS 9 expected credit loss model for Dutch residential mortgages (model identifier MDL-07, model name ECL-MORT-NL, model version 3.2) and follows the RDS template in Annex A of the Model Documentation Standard (MRM-STD-021). The RDS serves the re-estimation, annual recalibration and back-testing of the probability of default (PD), loss given default (LGD), exposure at default (EAD) and prepayment components and of the staging module of the model. Its scope is the residential mortgage portfolio of the Bank and of its wholly owned mortgage label subsidiary in the Netherlands, comprising owner-occupied mortgage loans with and without a National Mortgage Guarantee (NHG), together with binding mortgage offers and undisbursed construction deposits, which are loan commitments within the scope of the IFRS 9 impairment requirements. Buy-to-let mortgages are managed in the commercial real estate portfolio and are outside the scope. The model output is used to measure the 12-month and lifetime loss allowance for financial reporting under IFRS 9 and for the related IFRS 7 disclosures; secondary uses are the quarterly cost-of-risk reporting against the credit risk appetite and the IFRS 9 projections in the ICAAP and the EU-wide stress test. Although the model is a statistical model with fixed logic, its output is used for financial reporting and risk measurement, and it is therefore managed as a model across the full model lifecycle under the Model Risk Management Policy (MRM-POL-001).

sections.heading: Observation period
sections.text: The frozen RDS (version RDS-ECLM-2026-v1.0) consists of month-end snapshots from 31 January 2012 to 31 December 2026 (180 reference dates) at loan-part level, with an obligor-level aggregation for the PD component, and contains 76.4 million loan-part-months and 41.2 million obligor-months, covering 812,400 unique loan parts and 402,600 unique obligors (households). It contains 21,340 obligor default events after merging 1,105 re-defaults within 12 months of a cure, of which 17,450 workouts were closed by 31 December 2026 (11,020 cures and 6,430 liquidations). The prepayment sub-sample records 188,900 full redemptions and 1.46 million partial prepayments. The observed annual obligor default rate ranges from 1.12% (2013) to 0.29% (2021), with a long-run average of 0.63% over 2012–2026 and 0.41% in 2026. At the latest reference date, 31 December 2026, the portfolio comprises 262,800 obligors and 451,300 loan parts with a gross carrying amount of EUR 64.8 billion and EUR 1.9 billion of loan commitments.

sections.heading: Choice of observation window
sections.text: The window starts in January 2012, the first month for which the mortgage core system (MCS) provides complete loan-part history after the 2011 system migration; earlier data from the legacy system lack contractual repayment schedules and were not migrated. The 15-year window covers the Dutch housing market downturn of 2012–2013, the subsequent recovery, the COVID-19 period with payment holidays and the 2022–2023 interest rate increase with a nominal house price correction of about 5%, and therefore includes a full economic cycle with both adverse and benign years. The window exceeds the minimum of five years in FIN-STD-200 §11.2 and supports both the estimation of the relationship between default rates and macroeconomic conditions and the point-in-time calibration on recent years. Historical conditions that are not relevant for future cash flows are adjusted for rather than silently retained: the 2012–2014 data reflect the pre-2013 underwriting regime with interest-only loans up to 100% of market value, which is captured by product-type and origination-cohort variables, and the effect of the 2020 COVID-19 payment holidays on arrears is neutralised as described in section 3.3.1.

sections.heading: Development, recalibration and back-testing windows
sections.text: Within the RDS, the PD hazard model is estimated on reference dates January 2014 – December 2023, with a random 30% obligor hold-out as out-of-sample sample, January 2024 – December 2025 is reserved as out-of-time sample, and the 12-month point-in-time calibration uses the default rates observed in the calendar years 2024–2026. The LGD cure and loss-given-liquidation components are estimated on defaults from January 2012 to December 2023 with closed workouts, and the forced-sale discount is calibrated on 2,940 forced and assisted sales between 2016 and 2026. The prepayment model is estimated on January 2015 – December 2026, as prepayment reason codes are incomplete before 2015 (deficiency DD-05). Loss rates are applied only to groups defined in the same way as the groups on which they were observed: the LGD pools (NHG status, indexed LTV band and time in default) and the prepayment pools (product type, remaining fixed-rate period and penalty-free headroom) are identical in the RDS and in the production ECL engine, and each pool is linked to the current indexed LTV and interest rate data at the reporting date.

sections.heading: Target variable and outcome horizon
sections.text: The PD target is the occurrence of an obligor default under CR-STD-110 within 12 months after the reference date, used in a discrete-time hazard framework in which the 12-month hazards are chained into a lifetime term structure together with the competing prepayment hazard. The outcome horizon of the lifetime term structure is the remaining contractual maturity of each loan part, with a maximum of 30 years; mortgage contracts contain no extension options, and the RDS does not extend the horizon beyond the contractual maturity even where loans are refinanced in practice. The portfolio contains no revolving facilities, so the behavioural measurement period of IFRS 9 paragraph 5.5.20 does not apply; construction deposits are drawn under a fixed contractual schedule and binding offers expire after six months. The LGD target is the realised economic loss, being the exposure at default less discounted recoveries plus discounted directly attributable costs, divided by the exposure at default, with discounting at the effective interest rate of the loan part. The prepayment target is the monthly single mortality rate of full and partial redemptions per loan part.

sections.text: Not applicable: the default flag in the RDS follows CR-STD-110 without deviation from 1 January 2016, and the approximation for 2012–2015 required by CR-STD-110 §9.3 is documented in section 3.3.5 rather than treated as a deviation. sections.heading: Past-due criterion and days-past-due counting
sections.text: An obligor is in default when the materiality threshold of EUR 100 (absolute component) and 1% (relative component) has been exceeded for more than 90 consecutive days, or when the obligor is considered unlikely to pay under section 3.4; no more lagging criterion than 90 days past due is used. The days-past-due counter starts on the first day on which both components of the materiality threshold are exceeded and is reset to zero when either component is no longer exceeded. Any amount of principal, interest or fees not paid on its due date is a past due amount, and where the payment schedule has been modified, for example after a forbearance measure, days past due are counted against the modified schedule. Instalments deferred under the 2020 COVID-19 payment holidays, which met the general payment moratorium criteria of EBA/GL/2020/02, were not counted as past due, and the reasons for each deferral were reviewed by Collections for indications of unlikeliness to pay. Days past due are counted daily in the mortgage core system for all obligors, and for the monthly RDS snapshots the date of default is taken from the daily counter, i.e. the date on which the past due criterion was actually met, and not from the snapshot date. Technical past due situations are recognised only in the cases listed in paragraph 23 of EBA/GL/2016/07, in practice direct-debit execution failures attributable to the Bank or the payment system and payment allocation errors; the 1,318 technical past due cases in the RDS are not counted as defaults.

sections.heading: Materiality threshold and date of application
sections.text: The absolute component is compared with the sum of all past due amounts owed by the obligor to the Bank and its subsidiaries, and the relative component equals that sum divided by the obligor's total on-balance-sheet exposure to the Bank and its subsidiaries, excluding equity exposures. The thresholds are the single threshold set by the ECB for all significant institutions in Regulation (EU) 2018/1845 for retail exposures, with the relative component at the level of 1%. The regulatory threshold has been applied in the source systems from 1 November 2020 (DoD implementation release DOD-2020-R3); between 1 January 2016 and 31 October 2020 the production counter used the Bank's former internal threshold of EUR 250 without relative component. In the RDS the default flag for 2016–2020 is recomputed from the daily arrears ledger with the regulatory threshold, and the variable MAT_REGIME identifies for every default event whether it was identified under the recomputed or the production regulatory threshold. The recomputation changed 0.7% of the default events, mainly by bringing forward default dates of obligors with arrears between EUR 100 and EUR 250 (deficiency DD-02).

sections.heading: Level of application, joint obligations and contagion
sections.text: Default is identified at obligor level: an obligor is a household, i.e. the one or two borrowers jointly liable for a mortgage loan, and when the obligor defaults all its loan parts and any other credit obligations to the Bank and its subsidiaries are flagged as defaulted without additional expert judgement. The obligor level reflects the Bank's risk management practice, in which arrears management, forbearance and collections are organised per household, and it has been applied unchanged over the whole observation period. Because default is applied at obligor level, the materiality threshold is calculated at obligor level, and a joint obligation of two borrowers is treated as a separate obligor in the threshold calculation, distinct from the individual obligations of each borrower. Joint credit obligations and contagion between connected obligors are treated in accordance with CR-STD-110 §4.3 and section 8 of EBA/GL/2016/07. Obligor-related UTP indications such as bankruptcy or admission to the statutory debt rescheduling regime for natural persons (WSNP) always lead to default of all exposures of the obligor.

sections.heading: Probation, cure and multiple defaults
sections.text: An obligor returns to non-default status only after at least three months in which no default trigger applies and after Collections has assessed, on the basis of payment behaviour and income information during the probation period, that the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent. For defaults caused by a distressed restructuring the probation period is at least 12 months from the latest of the restructuring date, the end of any grace period and the date of default, and return additionally requires a material payment equal to the amount previously past due or written off, regular payments under the new schedule, no past due amount, no UTP indication and no remaining doubt about full repayment. The probation start date and probation status are recorded for every default event in the fields PROB_START_DT and PROB_STATUS of the Default Register and are carried into the RDS. Where an obligor defaults again within 12 months after returning to non-default status, both events are merged into a single default event starting at the first date of default; 1,105 such merges were applied in the RDS and are identified by the linking key DEF_EPISODE_ID. Re-default rates are analysed annually by Credit Risk Management per default trigger; in 2026 the 12-month re-default rate after cure was 8.4% for past-due defaults and 13.9% after distressed restructuring, which did not lead to a proposal for longer probation periods.

sections.heading: Historical approximation of the default flag
sections.text: Default flag components are captured in the source systems from 1 January 2016; for January 2012 – December 2015 the default flag is approximated from the arrears ledger (more than 90 days past due on amounts above EUR 100 and 1%, recomputed from monthly arrears amounts) and from the restructuring and foreclosure indicators of the collections system. Probation periods cannot be reconstructed for 2012–2015; for this period a return to non-default is approximated by three consecutive monthly snapshots without arrears, including for defaults after distressed restructuring, for which the 12-month probation cannot be observed. On the overlap year 2016, in which both the approximated and the full flag are available, the approximation identifies 3.2% fewer default events than the full definition, mainly because non-accrual and case-by-case UTP triggers are not observable before 2016. The approximation affects the long-run average default rate used for the reversion of the PD term structures and the LGD development sample, but not the point-in-time calibration on 2024–2026; it is recorded as deficiency DD-01 in section 6.2 and as limitation L-03 in the MDD.

sections.heading: Default definition register and consistency across systems
sections.text: The Default Register maintained by Credit Risk Management under CR-STD-110 contains the register of current and past default definitions, which for the mortgage portfolio records the pre-2016 definition, the 2016 definition (approved by the Group Risk Committee on 17 December 2015) and the 2020 definition implementing EBA/GL/2016/07 and the regulatory materiality threshold (approved on 22 September 2020, implemented on 1 November 2020), each with scope, approving body, dates and a description of the changes. The Default Register is the authoritative source of the default status, which is propagated daily to the mortgage core system, the collections system, the Risk Data Hub and the finance subledger, so that all exposures of a defaulted obligor are flagged as defaulted in all relevant IT systems of the Bank and its mortgage label subsidiary. The default flags used for IFRS 9 and for IRB purposes are reconciled quarterly between the Risk Data Hub and the finance subledger; the reconciliation for 31 December 2026 showed no unexplained differences.

sections.heading: Automatic unlikeliness-to-pay triggers
sections.text: The following UTP triggers lead to default without further assessment (CR-STD-110 §6.1): non-accrued status, in which interest is no longer recognised in the income statement because of a decrease in credit quality; any Stage 3 loss allowance or other specific credit risk adjustment resulting from a significant perceived decline in credit quality; the sale of the obligation at a credit-related economic loss above 5%; a distressed restructuring with a diminished financial obligation above 1%; bankruptcy or admission to the WSNP regime; and the forced sale of the property initiated by the Bank. Stage 1 and Stage 2 allowances reflect losses on exposures not individually identified as impaired and are not treated as specific credit risk adjustments, so they do not trigger default. Every exposure classified as credit-impaired (Stage 3) under IFRS 9 is in default, and the exceptions in paragraph 39 of EBA/GL/2016/07 are not used because Stage 3 is defined as the set of defaulted exposures. Each trigger is mapped to a source-system field: non-accrual to MCS.ACCRUAL_STATUS, specific adjustments to the stage of the finance subledger allowance, sale losses to the sale module of the Default Register, distressed restructuring to FBM.DFO_PCT of the forbearance module, bankruptcy and WSNP to the legal status in the collections system and forced sale to CMS.FORECLOSURE_FLAG.

sections.heading: Case-by-case unlikeliness-to-pay indicators
sections.text: The following indicators lead to a case-by-case assessment by the Collections Intensive Care team, completed within 30 days of detection: a significant decline in household income (for example unemployment or divorce reported in the arrears dialogue), fraud, multiple forbearance measures, default of a connected obligor, arrears on other credit obligations registered with the Dutch credit register BKR, and repeated arrears of more than 60 days. These indicators apply to all business lines and legal entities that hold residential mortgages, which are located only in the Netherlands, and each indicator is specified either as an automatic trigger or as a case-by-case indicator. The outcome of each case-by-case assessment, with its rationale, is recorded in the collections system in field UTP_ASSESS_OUTCOME; in 2026, 3,412 assessments were completed, of which 1,086 led to a default classification. A lower internal materiality threshold is not used as an additional UTP trigger, and the triggers and indicators are applied identically in the RDS construction and in production, so that they are documented and applied consistently over the period since 2016.

sections.heading: Forbearance, distressed restructuring and sales
sections.text: For every forbearance measure the forbearance module calculates the diminished financial obligation as (NPV0 − NPV1)/NPV0, where NPV0 and NPV1 are the net present values of the expected cash flows before and after the measure, both discounted at the original effective interest rate; a measure with a diminished financial obligation above 1% is a distressed restructuring and leads to default. All exposures classified as forborne non-performing are classified as defaulted. No residential mortgage credit obligations were sold during the observation period; transfers to the Bank's RMBS and covered bond vehicles do not lead to derecognition.

sections.heading: Source systems and data domains
sections.text: The RDS is built from the following source systems, each mapped to a data domain of the Group Data Catalogue with exactly one registered Data Owner: the mortgage core system MCS (domain Mortgage Loans, Data Owner Head of Mortgage Operations), the collections system COLL (domain Collections and Recoveries, Head of Retail Collections), the collateral management system CMS (domain Collateral, Head of Credit Risk Operations), the Default Register DEFREG (domain Credit Risk Status, Head of Credit Risk Management), the finance subledger FSL (domain Finance, Head of Finance Reporting) and the scenario store ESS (domain Macroeconomic Scenarios, Head of Enterprise Stress Testing). Extractions are taken from the Risk Data Hub (RDH), which stores daily and month-end snapshots of the source systems; the RDS uses the month-end snapshots with reference dates 31 January 2012 – 31 December 2026, extracted on 12 March 2027. Changes to the definition, source or transformation of a data element used by the model are approved by the Data Owner and notified to the model owner in advance through the RDH change calendar.

sections.heading: Lineage and transformations
sections.text: Lineage from source system field to RDS variable is documented for every variable in the data dictionary (Annex A) and in the lineage tool of the Group Data Catalogue, including the eleven discarded source fields used only to construct retained variables, such as the individual borrower incomes used to derive the household loan-to-income ratio. For each variable the lineage identifies the source system and fields, the intermediate stores (RDH staging and RDH core), each transformation, filter, join and aggregation with a reference to the build script and line range in the repository, and the extraction frequency and timing (month-end data available on the fifth business day). The same RDH tables feed the production ECL engine; the comparison of development and production lineage performed for version 3.2 found one difference, namely that the engine reads the indexed collateral value from CMS instead of recomputing it, whose effect on model outputs was quantified in the implementation report EVD-07-IMPL. The RDH data architecture supports daily and month-end aggregation of the mortgage risk data and remained within its service levels during the 2020 and 2022 stress periods, when additional monthly ECL runs were produced for management. Data taxonomies follow the Group Data Catalogue, which uses consistent customer, obligor, contract and loan-part identifiers and naming conventions across MCS, COLL, CMS, DEFREG and FSL. The data are aggregated on a largely automated basis by scheduled RDH jobs, which minimises the probability of errors.

sections.heading: Manual interventions and external data
sections.text: Two manual interventions exist in the data flow and are identified explicitly in the lineage: the monthly upload of the Intensive Care watchlist from the Collections workflow tool, a registered end-user computing application (EUC-COLL-017), and the expert mapping table of historical product codes to current product types (file product_map_v3.csv under version control). The watchlist upload is reconciled on record count and obligor keys to the source list by a second person in Collections before loading, and the product mapping table is documented as expert judgement EJ-RDS-02 under MRM-STD-023. External data enter the lineage at the point of receipt within the Bank and are recorded with provider, data product and delivery date: the CBS/Kadaster price index of existing owner-occupied dwellings (monthly delivery), the AVM indexation of property values of an external provider (quarterly data product 'Residential Index NL', delivery of 15 January 2027), BKR registrations, and NHG claim statuses from the Stichting Waarborgfonds Eigen Woningen. The AVM indexation is supplied by the external provider under contract VC-2023-114, which specifies delivery timelines and data quality commitments.

sections.heading: Critical data elements and metadata
sections.text: All 38 model input variables and the eight data elements used to construct the target variables (default flag, default date, probation status, exposure at default, recovery cash flows, recovery costs, write-off amount and prepayment amount) are designated as critical data elements. Each critical data element has a business definition, a technical definition and at least one data quality rule for each applicable dimension of MRM-STD-022 §3, recorded in Annex A and in the Group Data Catalogue, and the reason is recorded where a dimension does not apply. Metadata for every data element (business and technical definition, type and format, permitted values, unit and currency, source, Data Owner, update frequency and classification) are recorded in the Group Data Catalogue. The critical data elements were reconciled against the source systems and the general ledger in the annual reconciliation of February 2027, and the three unexplained differences found were recorded as data quality issues (section 6.1 of EVD-07-DQ).

sections.heading: Macroeconomic, collateral and borrower information
sections.text: Macroeconomic history (GDP, unemployment rate, house price index, mortgage interest rates and 3-month Euribor) for 2000–2026 and the scenario paths for 2027–2031 are taken from the ESS scenario store of Enterprise Stress Testing, which also supplies the scenarios used in the financial plan, the capital plan and the ICAAP. Property values are recorded in CMS with valuation date, valuation method (full appraisal, desktop valuation, AVM or indexation), lien rank and the link to the secured loan parts, and meet the data quality rules of MRM-STD-022. Every property is valued independently at origination by a certified appraiser, and values are monitored through quarterly statistical indexation and reviewed at least every three years, as required by CR-POL-001 §8.3. The RDS combines borrower-specific information (payment history, loan terms, income at origination and collateral), portfolio information (vintage and product mix) and macroeconomic history and forecasts, so that the model draws on a wide range of reasonable and supportable information about past events, current conditions and forecasts that is available without undue cost or effort. For every loan part the RDS retains the origination date, the 12-month PD at origination and the lifetime PD curve expected at origination, which are required for the SICR assessment.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Exclusion E1: loan-part-months with an incomplete contractual schedule after the 2011 migration (January–June 2012), 1.9 million loan-part-months (2.5%) and 610 default events; the impact analysis in section 5.3 concludes that the effect on representativeness is immaterial. Exclusion E2: staff mortgages with non-market conditions, 0.63 million loan-part-months (0.8%) and 41 default events, excluded from estimation but scored in production; section 5.3 concludes that their risk profile is covered by the model. Exclusion E3: 96 default events with confirmed origination fraud, excluded from the LGD sample only (0.6% of LGD observations). Exclusion E4: 15,300 duplicate loan-part-months created by the 2019 core system release (0.02%). Each exclusion is justified, quantified and assessed for its effect on representativeness; no exclusion exceeds 5% of records or exposure in any segment, the largest being 4.1% of loan-part-months in the pre-2013 interest-only segment caused by E1, so that no approval by the model owner under MRM-STD-022 §5.3 is required. Defaulted, cured, forborne and written-off loan parts are retained, so that the exclusions do not remove records in a way that could bias the ECL estimate.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: The treatment of missing values is documented per variable in Annex C and distinguishes values missing at random (for example the energy label, not recorded for 18% of properties), structurally missing values (for example the NHG claim amount for loans without NHG) and values missing because of a data deficiency (the original valuation for 5.9% of loan parts originated before 2008, deficiency DD-03). Missing original valuations are imputed by deflating the 2008 municipal WOZ value with the house price index to the origination month, a reproducible method implemented in build script impute_valuation.py; the share of imputed values is 5.9% of loan parts and 3.1% of exposure, and re-estimating the LTV coefficients without imputed records changes the portfolio PD by less than 0.5%. Outliers are identified with documented rules applied identically in development and production, namely indexed LTV above 200%, loan-to-income above 12 and interest rates outside 0–12%, and values are capped at the 99.5th percentile (LTV 175%, loan-to-income 9.5), which affects 0.3% of records and changes the modelled ECL by +0.2%. Missing values and outliers in the target variables are not imputed: 212 default events without a default date were investigated with Collections and corrected at source in the Default Register, and 38 closed workouts with a realised LGD below −20% were verified against the recovery ledger, of which 31 were confirmed as penalty interest and cost reimbursements and retained and seven were corrected at source.

sections.heading: Representativeness
sections.text: Representativeness of the RDS for the portfolio at 31 December 2026 is assessed on risk-driver distributions and on default-rate levels, with the detailed tables in Annex B; this covers the appropriateness dimension of MRM-STD-022 §3.6. The PSI of the development sample (2014–2023) against the December 2026 portfolio is 0.07 for the behavioural score and between 0.01 and 0.14 for the other drivers; the only amber value is indexed LTV (0.14), reflecting the house price increases since 2023 that moved the portfolio towards lower LTV bands. On default-rate levels, the observed 12-month default rate of the calibration window 2024–2026 (0.40%) is compared with that of the development window (0.66%); the difference reflects the benign current conditions and is the reason why the point-in-time calibration uses 2024–2026 rather than the development window, in line with FIN-STD-200 §6.3. Qualitatively, the product mix (declining share of interest-only and growing share of annuity loans), the underwriting standards (LTV cap reduced stepwise to 100% by 2018 and loan-to-income norms), collection policies and the legal environment have changed over the window; these changes are captured by product, origination-cohort and LTV variables. All products, NHG and non-NHG loans and origination cohorts up to December 2026 are represented in the RDS, so no segment of the current portfolio lacks development data.

sections.heading: Data quality assessment
sections.text: A data quality assessment of the frozen RDS was performed before the re-estimation for version 3.2 in accordance with MRM-STD-022 §5.1, and its full results are reported in the data quality assessment report EVD-07-DQ. The 46 critical data elements were assessed on completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness, and on validity, uniqueness and appropriateness where relevant, using 214 rules with amber and red thresholds at least as strict as the defaults of MRM-STD-022 §4.3. Results: 209 rules are green, four amber and one red (completeness of the original valuation, deficiency DD-03). The RDS reconciles to the general ledger for the gross carrying amount at every quarter-end from Q1 2016 within 0.05%, and to the mortgage core system for record counts per reference date without difference. The assessment concluded that the RDS is fit for the intended use of re-estimating and recalibrating model version 3.2, subject to the treatments in section 6.2, and was signed off by the model developer and the model owner on 26 March 2027. The same rules run in the Group DQ monitoring tool on the monthly production input data of the ECL engine, so that data quality in production can be compared with data quality at development.

sections.heading: Lawful basis and purposes of processing
sections.text: The RDS contains personal data of borrowers and is processed for three purposes recorded in the Record of Processing under processing activity RoP-FIN-0212 'Credit loss provisioning models – residential mortgages': development and recalibration, independent validation, and the quarterly application of the model in the ECL engine. The lawful basis, recorded before processing started, is Article 6(1)(c) GDPR for the application of the model, based on the Bank's legal obligations to prepare financial statements under Book 2 of the Dutch Civil Code and IFRS as adopted in the EU, and Article 6(1)(f) GDPR for development and validation, supported by legitimate interest assessment LIA-2025-031 approved by the Privacy Office on 14 October 2025. The data were collected for the administration of the mortgage contract, and their reuse for model development was assessed as compatible under Article 6(4) GDPR in compatibility assessment CA-2025-017, which considers the link between the purposes, the context of collection, the nature of the data, the possible consequences for data subjects and the pseudonymisation applied. The model inventory record of MDL-07 references processing activity RoP-FIN-0212 and DPIA-2025-064.

sections.heading: Personal data attributes and minimisation
sections.text: The RDS contains the following personal data attributes, each justified by its relevance to the model purpose: pseudonymised customer and obligor keys (linking of loan parts and households), gross household income at origination (loan-to-income ratio), number of borrowers, payment and arrears history, loan terms and the four-digit postcode of the property (collateral indexation). Direct identifiers such as names, addresses, citizen service numbers, dates of birth and contact details are not included, and the extraction selects fields on an allow-list reviewed by the Privacy Office, so that by default only data necessary for the purpose are processed, retained for a limited period and accessible to a limited group. For each attribute the data dictionary in Annex A states its purpose in the model, the lawful basis, the pseudonymisation applied and the retention period. Special categories of personal data are not processed: the free-text arrears reasons and the reason codes 'illness' and 'disability' of the collections system, which could reveal health data, are removed in the extraction, and the RDS contains no data on health, ethnic origin or religion.

sections.heading: Pseudonymisation, security and retention
sections.text: Development and validation use pseudonymised data: customer, obligor and contract numbers are replaced by keyed HMAC-SHA-256 tokens whose key is held by the Group Data Office as data custodian, separately from the modelling team. The RDS is held in the approved secure analytics environment SAE-Risk with role-based access for 14 named users of IFRS 9 Modelling and Model Validation, encryption at rest and access logging. No personal data are transferred outside the EEA; the analytics environment and its backups are located in the Bank's data centres in the Netherlands. Compliance with the GDPR principles for the model data can be demonstrated through the Record of Processing entry, the DPIA, the legitimate interest assessment and the compatibility assessment, which are stored with the model documentation.

sections.heading: Fair treatment and proxy screening
sections.text: No protected attributes, such as gender, nationality, ethnic origin, marital status or age, are included as model drivers, and all candidate variables were screened for proxy effects. The proxy screening of the 38 input variables against gender and age band, run by the data custodian in a separate controlled environment using Cramér's V and rank correlations, identified the four-digit postcode as a potential proxy; the postcode is therefore used only for the regional house price indexation, aggregated to the 40 COROP regions, and not as a PD driver. Age is not used in the model; the remaining loan term, which correlates weakly with age (Spearman 0.31), is retained for its credit rationale as a determinant of the amortisation profile, as approved by Credit Risk Management on 20 January 2027. The results of the proxy screening are documented in Annex B of this document and in section 4.3.1 of the MDD.

sections.heading: Representativeness analyses
sections.text: Annex B contains the PSI tables per risk driver and PD band for the development sample against the portfolios at 31 December 2024, 2025 and 2026, the default rates per PD band and segment for 2014–2026, the comparison of product mix, origination cohorts and NHG share over time and the proxy screening results referred to in section 7.5. The largest driver shift is indexed LTV (PSI 0.14 at December 2026), and the share of loan parts with an indexed LTV above 90% fell from 21% in 2014 to 3% in 2026. Missing and special-value shares are compared per variable; no variable shows a change of more than two percentage points.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Annex C lists per variable the missing value type, the treatment, the share of affected records in development and in production at 31 December 2026 and the outlier rule with its cap or floor. The original valuation (5.9% missing, imputed), the energy label (18% missing at random, not used as a driver) and the NHG claim amount (structurally missing for non-NHG loans) are the only variables with more than 1% missing values. The outlier rules for indexed LTV, loan-to-income and interest rates are implemented identically in build/outliers.py and in the production engine parameter table PARAM_ECL_MORT_V32.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This document is the reference data set (RDS) documentation of the IFRS 9 expected credit loss model for Dutch residential mortgages (model identifier MDL-07, model name ECL-MORT-NL, model version 3.2) and follows the RDS template in Annex A of the Model Documentation Standard (MRM-STD-021). The RDS serves the re-estimation, annual recalibration and back-testing of the probability of default (PD), loss given default (LGD), exposure at default (EAD) and prepayment components and of the staging module of the model. Its scope is the residential mortgage portfolio of the Bank and of its wholly owned mortgage label subsidiary in the Netherlands, comprising owner-occupied mortgage loans with and without a National Mortgage Guarantee (NHG), together with binding mortgage offers and undisbursed construction deposits, which are loan commitments within the scope of the IFRS 9 impairment requirements. Buy-to-let mortgages are managed in the commercial real estate portfolio and are outside the scope. The model output is used to measure the 12-month and lifetime loss allowance for financial reporting under IFRS 9 and for the related IFRS 7 disclosures; secondary uses are the quarterly cost-of-risk reporting against the credit risk appetite and the IFRS 9 projections in the ICAAP and the EU-wide stress test. Although the model is a statistical model with fixed logic, its output is used for financial reporting and risk measurement, and it is therefore managed as a model across the full model lifecycle under the Model Risk Management Policy (MRM-POL-001).

sections.heading: Observation period
sections.text: The frozen RDS (version RDS-ECLM-2026-v1.0) consists of month-end snapshots from 31 January 2012 to 31 December 2026 (180 reference dates) at loan-part level, with an obligor-level aggregation for the PD component, and contains 76.4 million loan-part-months and 41.2 million obligor-months, covering 812,400 unique loan parts and 402,600 unique obligors (households). It contains 21,340 obligor default events after merging 1,105 re-defaults within 12 months of a cure, of which 17,450 workouts were closed by 31 December 2026 (11,020 cures and 6,430 liquidations). The prepayment sub-sample records 188,900 full redemptions and 1.46 million partial prepayments. The observed annual obligor default rate ranges from 1.12% (2013) to 0.29% (2021), with a long-run average of 0.63% over 2012–2026 and 0.41% in 2026. At the latest reference date, 31 December 2026, the portfolio comprises 262,800 obligors and 451,300 loan parts with a gross carrying amount of EUR 64.8 billion and EUR 1.9 billion of loan commitments.

sections.heading: Choice of observation window
sections.text: The window starts in January 2012, the first month for which the mortgage core system (MCS) provides complete loan-part history after the 2011 system migration; earlier data from the legacy system lack contractual repayment schedules and were not migrated. The 15-year window covers the Dutch housing market downturn of 2012–2013, the subsequent recovery, the COVID-19 period with payment holidays and the 2022–2023 interest rate increase with a nominal house price correction of about 5%, and therefore includes a full economic cycle with both adverse and benign years. The window exceeds the minimum of five years in FIN-STD-200 §11.2 and supports both the estimation of the relationship between default rates and macroeconomic conditions and the point-in-time calibration on recent years. Historical conditions that are not relevant for future cash flows are adjusted for rather than silently retained: the 2012–2014 data reflect the pre-2013 underwriting regime with interest-only loans up to 100% of market value, which is captured by product-type and origination-cohort variables, and the effect of the 2020 COVID-19 payment holidays on arrears is neutralised as described in section 3.3.1.

sections.heading: Development, recalibration and back-testing windows
sections.text: Within the RDS, the PD hazard model is estimated on reference dates January 2014 – December 2023, with a random 30% obligor hold-out as out-of-sample sample, January 2024 – December 2025 is reserved as out-of-time sample, and the 12-month point-in-time calibration uses the default rates observed in the calendar years 2024–2026. The LGD cure and loss-given-liquidation components are estimated on defaults from January 2012 to December 2023 with closed workouts, and the forced-sale discount is calibrated on 2,940 forced and assisted sales between 2016 and 2026. The prepayment model is estimated on January 2015 – December 2026, as prepayment reason codes are incomplete before 2015 (deficiency DD-05). Loss rates are applied only to groups defined in the same way as the groups on which they were observed: the LGD pools (NHG status, indexed LTV band and time in default) and the prepayment pools (product type, remaining fixed-rate period and penalty-free headroom) are identical in the RDS and in the production ECL engine, and each pool is linked to the current indexed LTV and interest rate data at the reporting date.

sections.heading: Target variable and outcome horizon
sections.text: The PD target is the occurrence of an obligor default under CR-STD-110 within 12 months after the reference date, used in a discrete-time hazard framework in which the 12-month hazards are chained into a lifetime term structure together with the competing prepayment hazard. The outcome horizon of the lifetime term structure is the remaining contractual maturity of each loan part, with a maximum of 30 years; mortgage contracts contain no extension options, and the RDS does not extend the horizon beyond the contractual maturity even where loans are refinanced in practice. The portfolio contains no revolving facilities, so the behavioural measurement period of IFRS 9 paragraph 5.5.20 does not apply; construction deposits are drawn under a fixed contractual schedule and binding offers expire after six months. The LGD target is the realised economic loss, being the exposure at default less discounted recoveries plus discounted directly attributable costs, divided by the exposure at default, with discounting at the effective interest rate of the loan part. The prepayment target is the monthly single mortality rate of full and partial redemptions per loan part.

sections.heading: Past-due criterion and days-past-due counting
sections.text: An obligor is in default when the materiality threshold of EUR 100 (absolute component) and 1% (relative component) has been exceeded for more than 90 consecutive days, or when the obligor is considered unlikely to pay under section 3.4; no more lagging criterion than 90 days past due is used. The days-past-due counter starts on the first day on which both components of the materiality threshold are exceeded and is reset to zero when either component is no longer exceeded. Any amount of principal, interest or fees not paid on its due date is a past due amount, and where the payment schedule has been modified, for example after a forbearance measure, days past due are counted against the modified schedule. Instalments deferred under the 2020 COVID-19 payment holidays, which met the general payment moratorium criteria of EBA/GL/2020/02, were not counted as past due, and the reasons for each deferral were reviewed by Collections for indications of unlikeliness to pay. Days past due are counted daily in the mortgage core system for all obligors, and for the monthly RDS snapshots the date of default is taken from the daily counter, i.e. the date on which the past due criterion was actually met, and not from the snapshot date. Technical past due situations are recognised only in the cases listed in paragraph 23 of EBA/GL/2016/07, in practice direct-debit execution failures attributable to the Bank or the payment system and payment allocation errors; the 1,318 technical past due cases in the RDS are not counted as defaults.

sections.heading: Materiality threshold and date of application
sections.text: The absolute component is compared with the sum of all past due amounts owed by the obligor to the Bank and its subsidiaries, and the relative component equals that sum divided by the obligor's total on-balance-sheet exposure to the Bank and its subsidiaries, excluding equity exposures. The thresholds are the single threshold set by the ECB for all significant institutions in Regulation (EU) 2018/1845 for retail exposures, with the relative component at the level of 1%. The regulatory threshold has been applied in the source systems from 1 November 2020 (DoD implementation release DOD-2020-R3); between 1 January 2016 and 31 October 2020 the production counter used the Bank's former internal threshold of EUR 250 without relative component. In the RDS the default flag for 2016–2020 is recomputed from the daily arrears ledger with the regulatory threshold, and the variable MAT_REGIME identifies for every default event whether it was identified under the recomputed or the production regulatory threshold. The recomputation changed 0.7% of the default events, mainly by bringing forward default dates of obligors with arrears between EUR 100 and EUR 250 (deficiency DD-02).

sections.heading: Level of application, joint obligations and contagion
sections.text: Default is identified at obligor level: an obligor is a household, i.e. the one or two borrowers jointly liable for a mortgage loan, and when the obligor defaults all its loan parts and any other credit obligations to the Bank and its subsidiaries are flagged as defaulted without additional expert judgement. The obligor level reflects the Bank's risk management practice, in which arrears management, forbearance and collections are organised per household, and it has been applied unchanged over the whole observation period. Because default is applied at obligor level, the materiality threshold is calculated at obligor level, and a joint obligation of two borrowers is treated as a separate obligor in the threshold calculation, distinct from the individual obligations of each borrower. Joint credit obligations and contagion between connected obligors are treated in accordance with CR-STD-110 §4.3 and section 8 of EBA/GL/2016/07. Obligor-related UTP indications such as bankruptcy or admission to the statutory debt rescheduling regime for natural persons (WSNP) always lead to default of all exposures of the obligor.

sections.heading: Probation, cure and multiple defaults
sections.text: An obligor returns to non-default status only after at least three months in which no default trigger applies and after Collections has assessed, on the basis of payment behaviour and income information during the probation period, that the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent. For defaults caused by a distressed restructuring the probation period is at least 12 months from the latest of the restructuring date, the end of any grace period and the date of default, and return additionally requires a material payment equal to the amount previously past due or written off, regular payments under the new schedule, no past due amount, no UTP indication and no remaining doubt about full repayment. The probation start date and probation status are recorded for every default event in the fields PROB_START_DT and PROB_STATUS of the Default Register and are carried into the RDS. Where an obligor defaults again within 12 months after returning to non-default status, both events are merged into a single default event starting at the first date of default; 1,105 such merges were applied in the RDS and are identified by the linking key DEF_EPISODE_ID. Re-default rates are analysed annually by Credit Risk Management per default trigger; in 2026 the 12-month re-default rate after cure was 8.4% for past-due defaults and 13.9% after distressed restructuring, which did not lead to a proposal for longer probation periods.

sections.heading: Historical approximation of the default flag
sections.text: Default flag components are captured in the source systems from 1 January 2016; for January 2012 – December 2015 the default flag is approximated from the arrears ledger (more than 90 days past due on amounts above EUR 100 and 1%, recomputed from monthly arrears amounts) and from the restructuring and foreclosure indicators of the collections system. Probation periods cannot be reconstructed for 2012–2015; for this period a return to non-default is approximated by three consecutive monthly snapshots without arrears, including for defaults after distressed restructuring, for which the 12-month probation cannot be observed. On the overlap year 2016, in which both the approximated and the full flag are available, the approximation identifies 3.2% fewer default events than the full definition, mainly because non-accrual and case-by-case UTP triggers are not observable before 2016. The approximation affects the long-run average default rate used for the reversion of the PD term structures and the LGD development sample, but not the point-in-time calibration on 2024–2026; it is recorded as deficiency DD-01 in section 6.2 and as limitation L-03 in the MDD. The RDS default flag is reconciled with the production default flag for January 2016 – December 2026, when both are available: 99.4% of default events match on obligor and default month, and the remaining 0.6% are explained by the recomputed materiality regime (section 3.3.2) and by 38 retroactive corrections in the Default Register.

sections.heading: Default definition register and consistency across systems
sections.text: The Default Register maintained by Credit Risk Management under CR-STD-110 contains the register of current and past default definitions, which for the mortgage portfolio records the pre-2016 definition, the 2016 definition (approved by the Group Risk Committee on 17 December 2015) and the 2020 definition implementing EBA/GL/2016/07 and the regulatory materiality threshold (approved on 22 September 2020, implemented on 1 November 2020), each with scope, approving body, dates and a description of the changes. The Default Register is the authoritative source of the default status, which is propagated daily to the mortgage core system, the collections system, the Risk Data Hub and the finance subledger, so that all exposures of a defaulted obligor are flagged as defaulted in all relevant IT systems of the Bank and its mortgage label subsidiary. The default flags used for IFRS 9 and for IRB purposes are reconciled quarterly between the Risk Data Hub and the finance subledger; the reconciliation for 31 December 2026 showed no unexplained differences.

sections.heading: Automatic unlikeliness-to-pay triggers
sections.text: The following UTP triggers lead to default without further assessment (CR-STD-110 §6.1): non-accrued status, in which interest is no longer recognised in the income statement because of a decrease in credit quality; any Stage 3 loss allowance or other specific credit risk adjustment resulting from a significant perceived decline in credit quality; the sale of the obligation at a credit-related economic loss above 5%; a distressed restructuring with a diminished financial obligation above 1%; bankruptcy or admission to the WSNP regime; and the forced sale of the property initiated by the Bank. Stage 1 and Stage 2 allowances reflect losses on exposures not individually identified as impaired and are not treated as specific credit risk adjustments, so they do not trigger default. Every exposure classified as credit-impaired (Stage 3) under IFRS 9 is in default, and the exceptions in paragraph 39 of EBA/GL/2016/07 are not used because Stage 3 is defined as the set of defaulted exposures. Each trigger is mapped to a source-system field: non-accrual to MCS.ACCRUAL_STATUS, specific adjustments to the stage of the finance subledger allowance, sale losses to the sale module of the Default Register, distressed restructuring to FBM.DFO_PCT of the forbearance module, bankruptcy and WSNP to the legal status in the collections system and forced sale to CMS.FORECLOSURE_FLAG.

sections.heading: Case-by-case unlikeliness-to-pay indicators
sections.text: The following indicators lead to a case-by-case assessment by the Collections Intensive Care team, completed within 30 days of detection: a significant decline in household income (for example unemployment or divorce reported in the arrears dialogue), fraud, multiple forbearance measures, default of a connected obligor, arrears on other credit obligations registered with the Dutch credit register BKR, and repeated arrears of more than 60 days. These indicators apply to all business lines and legal entities that hold residential mortgages, which are located only in the Netherlands, and each indicator is specified either as an automatic trigger or as a case-by-case indicator. The outcome of each case-by-case assessment, with its rationale, is recorded in the collections system in field UTP_ASSESS_OUTCOME; in 2026, 3,412 assessments were completed, of which 1,086 led to a default classification. A lower internal materiality threshold is not used as an additional UTP trigger, and the triggers and indicators are applied identically in the RDS construction and in production, so that they are documented and applied consistently over the period since 2016.

sections.heading: Forbearance, distressed restructuring and sales
sections.text: For every forbearance measure the forbearance module calculates the diminished financial obligation as (NPV0 − NPV1)/NPV0, where NPV0 and NPV1 are the net present values of the expected cash flows before and after the measure, both discounted at the original effective interest rate; a measure with a diminished financial obligation above 1% is a distressed restructuring and leads to default. All exposures classified as forborne non-performing are classified as defaulted. No residential mortgage credit obligations were sold during the observation period; transfers to the Bank's RMBS and covered bond vehicles do not lead to derecognition.

sections.text: Automatic default identification (days-past-due counting, non-accrual, bankruptcy and WSNP register matching, forced-sale flags) runs daily in the source systems. Monthly RDS snapshots take the default status as recorded in the Default Register at the month-end cut-off, and default dates are taken from the daily counters. sections.heading: Source systems and data domains
sections.text: The RDS is built from the following source systems, each mapped to a data domain of the Group Data Catalogue with exactly one registered Data Owner: the mortgage core system MCS (domain Mortgage Loans, Data Owner Head of Mortgage Operations), the collections system COLL (domain Collections and Recoveries, Head of Retail Collections), the collateral management system CMS (domain Collateral, Head of Credit Risk Operations), the Default Register DEFREG (domain Credit Risk Status, Head of Credit Risk Management), the finance subledger FSL (domain Finance, Head of Finance Reporting) and the scenario store ESS (domain Macroeconomic Scenarios, Head of Enterprise Stress Testing). Extractions are taken from the Risk Data Hub (RDH), which stores daily and month-end snapshots of the source systems; the RDS uses the month-end snapshots with reference dates 31 January 2012 – 31 December 2026, extracted on 12 March 2027. Changes to the definition, source or transformation of a data element used by the model are approved by the Data Owner and notified to the model owner in advance through the RDH change calendar.

sections.heading: Lineage and transformations
sections.text: Lineage from source system field to RDS variable is documented for every variable in the data dictionary (Annex A) and in the lineage tool of the Group Data Catalogue, including the eleven discarded source fields used only to construct retained variables, such as the individual borrower incomes used to derive the household loan-to-income ratio. For each variable the lineage identifies the source system and fields, the intermediate stores (RDH staging and RDH core), each transformation, filter, join and aggregation with a reference to the build script and line range in the repository, and the extraction frequency and timing (month-end data available on the fifth business day). The same RDH tables feed the production ECL engine; the comparison of development and production lineage performed for version 3.2 found one difference, namely that the engine reads the indexed collateral value from CMS instead of recomputing it, whose effect on model outputs was quantified in the implementation report EVD-07-IMPL. The RDH data architecture supports daily and month-end aggregation of the mortgage risk data and remained within its service levels during the 2020 and 2022 stress periods, when additional monthly ECL runs were produced for management. Data taxonomies follow the Group Data Catalogue, which uses consistent customer, obligor, contract and loan-part identifiers and naming conventions across MCS, COLL, CMS, DEFREG and FSL. The data are aggregated on a largely automated basis by scheduled RDH jobs, which minimises the probability of errors.

sections.heading: Manual interventions and external data
sections.text: Two manual interventions exist in the data flow and are identified explicitly in the lineage: the monthly upload of the Intensive Care watchlist from the Collections workflow tool, a registered end-user computing application (EUC-COLL-017), and the expert mapping table of historical product codes to current product types (file product_map_v3.csv under version control). The watchlist upload is reconciled on record count and obligor keys to the source list by a second person in Collections before loading, and the product mapping table is documented as expert judgement EJ-RDS-02 under MRM-STD-023. External data enter the lineage at the point of receipt within the Bank and are recorded with provider, data product and delivery date: the CBS/Kadaster price index of existing owner-occupied dwellings (monthly delivery), the AVM indexation of property values of an external provider (quarterly data product 'Residential Index NL', delivery of 15 January 2027), BKR registrations, and NHG claim statuses from the Stichting Waarborgfonds Eigen Woningen. The AVM indexation is supplied by the external provider under contract VC-2023-114, which specifies delivery timelines and data quality commitments.

sections.heading: Critical data elements and metadata
sections.text: All 38 model input variables and the eight data elements used to construct the target variables (default flag, default date, probation status, exposure at default, recovery cash flows, recovery costs, write-off amount and prepayment amount) are designated as critical data elements. Each critical data element has a business definition, a technical definition and at least one data quality rule for each applicable dimension of MRM-STD-022 §3, recorded in Annex A and in the Group Data Catalogue, and the reason is recorded where a dimension does not apply. Metadata for every data element (business and technical definition, type and format, permitted values, unit and currency, source, Data Owner, update frequency and classification) are recorded in the Group Data Catalogue. The critical data elements were reconciled against the source systems and the general ledger in the annual reconciliation of February 2027, and the three unexplained differences found were recorded as data quality issues (section 6.1 of EVD-07-DQ).

sections.heading: Macroeconomic, collateral and borrower information
sections.text: Macroeconomic history (GDP, unemployment rate, house price index, mortgage interest rates and 3-month Euribor) for 2000–2026 and the scenario paths for 2027–2031 are taken from the ESS scenario store of Enterprise Stress Testing, which also supplies the scenarios used in the financial plan, the capital plan and the ICAAP. Property values are recorded in CMS with valuation date, valuation method (full appraisal, desktop valuation, AVM or indexation), lien rank and the link to the secured loan parts, and meet the data quality rules of MRM-STD-022. Every property is valued independently at origination by a certified appraiser, and values are monitored through quarterly statistical indexation and reviewed at least every three years, as required by CR-POL-001 §8.3. The RDS combines borrower-specific information (payment history, loan terms, income at origination and collateral), portfolio information (vintage and product mix) and macroeconomic history and forecasts, so that the model draws on a wide range of reasonable and supportable information about past events, current conditions and forecasts that is available without undue cost or effort. For every loan part the RDS retains the origination date, the 12-month PD at origination and the lifetime PD curve expected at origination, which are required for the SICR assessment.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Exclusion E1: loan-part-months with an incomplete contractual schedule after the 2011 migration (January–June 2012), 1.9 million loan-part-months (2.5%) and 610 default events; the impact analysis in section 5.3 concludes that the effect on representativeness is immaterial. Exclusion E2: staff mortgages with non-market conditions, 0.63 million loan-part-months (0.8%) and 41 default events, excluded from estimation but scored in production; section 5.3 concludes that their risk profile is covered by the model. Exclusion E3: 96 default events with confirmed origination fraud, excluded from the LGD sample only (0.6% of LGD observations). Exclusion E4: 15,300 duplicate loan-part-months created by the 2019 core system release (0.02%). Each exclusion is justified, quantified and assessed for its effect on representativeness; no exclusion exceeds 5% of records or exposure in any segment, the largest being 4.1% of loan-part-months in the pre-2013 interest-only segment caused by E1, so that no approval by the model owner under MRM-STD-022 §5.3 is required. Defaulted, cured, forborne and written-off loan parts are retained, so that the exclusions do not remove records in a way that could bias the ECL estimate.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: The treatment of missing values is documented per variable in Annex C and distinguishes values missing at random (for example the energy label, not recorded for 18% of properties), structurally missing values (for example the NHG claim amount for loans without NHG) and values missing because of a data deficiency (the original valuation for 5.9% of loan parts originated before 2008, deficiency DD-03). Missing original valuations are imputed by deflating the 2008 municipal WOZ value with the house price index to the origination month, a reproducible method implemented in build script impute_valuation.py; the share of imputed values is 5.9% of loan parts and 3.1% of exposure, and re-estimating the LTV coefficients without imputed records changes the portfolio PD by less than 0.5%. Outliers are identified with documented rules applied identically in development and production, namely indexed LTV above 200%, loan-to-income above 12 and interest rates outside 0–12%, and values are capped at the 99.5th percentile (LTV 175%, loan-to-income 9.5), which affects 0.3% of records and changes the modelled ECL by +0.2%. Missing values and outliers in the target variables are not imputed: 212 default events without a default date were investigated with Collections and corrected at source in the Default Register, and 38 closed workouts with a realised LGD below −20% were verified against the recovery ledger, of which 31 were confirmed as penalty interest and cost reimbursements and retained and seven were corrected at source.

sections.heading: Representativeness
sections.text: Representativeness of the RDS for the portfolio at 31 December 2026 is assessed on risk-driver distributions and on default-rate levels, with the detailed tables in Annex B; this covers the appropriateness dimension of MRM-STD-022 §3.6. The PSI of the development sample (2014–2023) against the December 2026 portfolio is 0.07 for the behavioural score and between 0.01 and 0.14 for the other drivers; the only amber value is indexed LTV (0.14), reflecting the house price increases since 2023 that moved the portfolio towards lower LTV bands. On default-rate levels, the observed 12-month default rate of the calibration window 2024–2026 (0.40%) is compared with that of the development window (0.66%); the difference reflects the benign current conditions and is the reason why the point-in-time calibration uses 2024–2026 rather than the development window, in line with FIN-STD-200 §6.3. Qualitatively, the product mix (declining share of interest-only and growing share of annuity loans), the underwriting standards (LTV cap reduced stepwise to 100% by 2018 and loan-to-income norms), collection policies and the legal environment have changed over the window; these changes are captured by product, origination-cohort and LTV variables. All products, NHG and non-NHG loans and origination cohorts up to December 2026 are represented in the RDS, so no segment of the current portfolio lacks development data.

sections.heading: Representativeness for other uses
sections.text: Not applicable: the model is not used outside the RDS population. The secondary uses in the ICAAP and the EU-wide stress test apply the model to the same portfolio under different macroeconomic scenarios and do not extend the model to other products or entities; their scenario-specific use is governed by the stress testing framework ERM-STD-300. Should the model be applied to another portfolio, for example buy-to-let loans, a representativeness analysis under this section would be performed and the change assessed under MRM-STD-050 as a change in the range of application.

sections.heading: Impact of exclusions
sections.text: Exclusion E1 slightly under-represents the pre-2013 interest-only segment in 2012; its effect on the default rate of the segment is −0.03 percentage points and on the average PD of the segment below 1%. Exclusion E2 has no measurable effect on the risk-driver distributions; staff mortgages are scored in production, and their observed default rate (0.21%) is below that of the portfolio. Exclusion E3 reduces the average realised LGD of the development sample by 0.1 percentage point, and E4 has no effect on distributions or default rates. The effect of all exclusions together on the modelled ECL at 31 December 2026 is −0.4%, and the overall conclusion is that the exclusions do not affect representativeness materially.

sections.heading: Data quality assessment
sections.text: A data quality assessment of the frozen RDS was performed before the re-estimation for version 3.2 in accordance with MRM-STD-022 §5.1, and its full results are reported in the data quality assessment report EVD-07-DQ. The 46 critical data elements were assessed on completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness, and on validity, uniqueness and appropriateness where relevant, using 214 rules with amber and red thresholds at least as strict as the defaults of MRM-STD-022 §4.3. Results: 209 rules are green, four amber and one red (completeness of the original valuation, deficiency DD-03). The RDS reconciles to the general ledger for the gross carrying amount at every quarter-end from Q1 2016 within 0.05%, and to the mortgage core system for record counts per reference date without difference. The assessment concluded that the RDS is fit for the intended use of re-estimating and recalibrating model version 3.2, subject to the treatments in section 6.2, and was signed off by the model developer and the model owner on 26 March 2027. The same rules run in the Group DQ monitoring tool on the monthly production input data of the ECL engine, so that data quality in production can be compared with data quality at development.

sections.heading: Data deficiencies

DD-05 (completeness, 2012–2014, prepayment reason codes): years excluded from the partial prepayment estimation; limitation L-08. sections.heading: Escalation and governance of data quality issues
sections.text: Data quality of the model data is managed in accordance with MRM-STD-022, as required by DATA-POL-001 §8.1. The red completeness result on the original valuation (DD-03) is a red breach on a critical data element of a Tier 1 model; it was escalated to Model Risk Management on 12 March 2027, within ten business days of detection on 3 March 2027, and reported to the Model Risk Committee on 25 March 2027. Being rated high in the Bank data issue register, the issue was also escalated to the Group Data Governance Committee on 18 March 2027. All residential mortgage loan parts of the Bank and its mortgage label subsidiary are captured, the completeness reconciliation shows no missing loan parts, and the known gaps (DD-03 and DD-04) are identified with their impact on the reliability of the ECL estimate. The controls over the ECL input data are part of the Finance internal control framework (key controls FIN-ECL-C04 to FIN-ECL-C09) and are tested annually by Internal Control to the same standard as the controls over accounting data.

sections.heading: Lawful basis and purposes of processing
sections.text: The RDS contains personal data of borrowers and is processed for three purposes recorded in the Record of Processing under processing activity RoP-FIN-0212 'Credit loss provisioning models – residential mortgages': development and recalibration, independent validation, and the quarterly application of the model in the ECL engine. The lawful basis, recorded before processing started, is Article 6(1)(c) GDPR for the application of the model, based on the Bank's legal obligations to prepare financial statements under Book 2 of the Dutch Civil Code and IFRS as adopted in the EU, and Article 6(1)(f) GDPR for development and validation, supported by legitimate interest assessment LIA-2025-031 approved by the Privacy Office on 14 October 2025. The data were collected for the administration of the mortgage contract, and their reuse for model development was assessed as compatible under Article 6(4) GDPR in compatibility assessment CA-2025-017, which considers the link between the purposes, the context of collection, the nature of the data, the possible consequences for data subjects and the pseudonymisation applied. The model inventory record of MDL-07 references processing activity RoP-FIN-0212 and DPIA-2025-064.

sections.heading: Personal data attributes and minimisation
sections.text: The RDS contains the following personal data attributes, each justified by its relevance to the model purpose: pseudonymised customer and obligor keys (linking of loan parts and households), gross household income at origination (loan-to-income ratio), number of borrowers, payment and arrears history, loan terms and the four-digit postcode of the property (collateral indexation). Direct identifiers such as names, addresses, citizen service numbers, dates of birth and contact details are not included, and the extraction selects fields on an allow-list reviewed by the Privacy Office, so that by default only data necessary for the purpose are processed, retained for a limited period and accessible to a limited group. For each attribute the data dictionary in Annex A states its purpose in the model, the lawful basis, the pseudonymisation applied and the retention period. Special categories of personal data are not processed: the free-text arrears reasons and the reason codes 'illness' and 'disability' of the collections system, which could reveal health data, are removed in the extraction, and the RDS contains no data on health, ethnic origin or religion.

sections.heading: Pseudonymisation, security and retention
sections.text: Development and validation use pseudonymised data: customer, obligor and contract numbers are replaced by keyed HMAC-SHA-256 tokens whose key is held by the Group Data Office as data custodian, separately from the modelling team. The RDS is held in the approved secure analytics environment SAE-Risk with role-based access for 14 named users of IFRS 9 Modelling and Model Validation, encryption at rest and access logging. Frozen RDS versions are retained in pseudonymised form for the life of the model and ten years after its decommissioning, as required by DATA-POL-001 §10.2, which the Privacy Office approved on 14 October 2025 (decision PO-2025-112) as an exception to the five-year period of PRIV-POL-001 §10.2; working snapshots are deleted after five years. No personal data are transferred outside the EEA; the analytics environment and its backups are located in the Bank's data centres in the Netherlands. Compliance with the GDPR principles for the model data can be demonstrated through the Record of Processing entry, the DPIA, the legitimate interest assessment and the compatibility assessment, which are stored with the model documentation.

sections.heading: Fair treatment and proxy screening
sections.text: No protected attributes, such as gender, nationality, ethnic origin, marital status or age, are included as model drivers, and all candidate variables were screened for proxy effects. The proxy screening of the 38 input variables against gender and age band, run by the data custodian in a separate controlled environment using Cramér's V and rank correlations, identified the four-digit postcode as a potential proxy; the postcode is therefore used only for the regional house price indexation, aggregated to the 40 COROP regions, and not as a PD driver. Age is not used in the model; the remaining loan term, which correlates weakly with age (Spearman 0.31), is retained for its credit rationale as a determinant of the amortisation profile, as approved by Credit Risk Management on 20 January 2027. The results of the proxy screening are documented in Annex B of this document and in section 4.3.1 of the MDD.

All extraction, exclusion, default flag construction and variable derivation steps are performed by the build code, no manual data manipulation is used, and the two manual inputs are version-controlled files documented under section 4.1.3. The build code was reviewed by a second developer who did not write it (merge request !218) before the RDS was submitted to Model Validation. The frozen RDS is stored read-only in SAE-Risk under version identifier RDS-ECLM-2026-v1.0, which is referenced in this document and in chapter 12 of the MDD.

sections.heading: Data dictionary and lineage
sections.text: Annex A states for all 38 input variables and eight target constituents the business definition, source system and field, transformation, lineage and critical data element designation, as required by MRM-STD-021 §4.6. Example IND_LTV: sum of the outstanding balances of all loan parts secured by the property divided by the indexed market value; sources MCS.OUTST_BAL and CMS.MARKET_VALUE with the quarterly AVM index; transformation build/ltv.py lines 40–96; critical data element; personal data: no. Example ARR_MAX_12M: maximum days past due of the obligor over the last 12 month-ends; source DEFREG.DPD_DAILY; transformation build/arrears.py lines 12–58; critical data element. Example DEF_PRUD: prudential default flag at obligor level per CR-STD-110, including MAT_REGIME and DEF_EPISODE_ID; source DEFREG; transformation build/default_flag.py; target constituent.

sections.heading: Representativeness analyses
sections.text: Annex B contains the PSI tables per risk driver and PD band for the development sample against the portfolios at 31 December 2024, 2025 and 2026, the default rates per PD band and segment for 2014–2026, the comparison of product mix, origination cohorts and NHG share over time and the proxy screening results referred to in section 7.5. The largest driver shift is indexed LTV (PSI 0.14 at December 2026), and the share of loan parts with an indexed LTV above 90% fell from 21% in 2014 to 3% in 2026. Missing and special-value shares are compared per variable; no variable shows a change of more than two percentage points.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Annex C lists per variable the missing value type, the treatment, the share of affected records in development and in production at 31 December 2026 and the outlier rule with its cap or floor. The original valuation (5.9% missing, imputed), the energy label (18% missing at random, not used as a driver) and the NHG claim amount (structurally missing for non-NHG loans) are the only variables with more than 1% missing values. The outlier rules for indexed LTV, loan-to-income and interest rates are implemented identically in build/outliers.py and in the production engine parameter table PARAM_ECL_MORT_V32.

sections.heading: Purpose, scope and intended use
sections.text: ECL-MORT-NL measures the loss allowance for expected credit losses on all Dutch residential mortgage loans of the Bank and its mortgage label subsidiary measured at amortised cost, and on the related loan commitments (binding mortgage offers); the portfolio contains no financial guarantee contracts, lease receivables or assets at fair value through other comprehensive income. For loan commitments, the date on which the customer accepts the binding offer, which makes the Bank party to an irrevocable commitment, is the date of initial recognition for impairment purposes and the reference point for the SICR assessment; the origination PD curve is fixed at that date. The model produces the 12-month and lifetime ECL per loan part at each month-end, the stage allocation, and the scenario-specific ECL used for the IFRS 7 sensitivity disclosures; secondary uses are the cost-of-risk projections in the financial plan, the ICAAP and the EU-wide stress test. Main users are Finance Reporting, which books the allowance, Credit Risk Management, which uses the stage distribution and cost of risk in the credit risk appetite reporting, and Enterprise Stress Testing. The expected loss and cost-of-risk metrics of the mortgage portfolio in the credit risk appetite statement are measured with the output of this registered and approved model. The model output is not used in decisions on individual customers: the stage allocation and loan-part ECL do not enter acceptance, pricing, limit or collections decisions, also not through third parties, so that no automated individual decision with legal or similarly significant effects within the meaning of Article 22 GDPR arises. At 31 December 2026 the portfolio comprises 451,300 loan parts of 262,800 obligors with a gross carrying amount of EUR 64.8 billion and EUR 1.9 billion of binding offers, and the loss allowance amounts to EUR 96.2 million, of which EUR 77.8 million modelled and EUR 18.4 million overlays.
