sections.heading: Materiality, approval and challenge of expert judgement; stage overrides
sections.text: Each judgement is classified by its impact on the ECL relative to the output without the judgement or the best statistical alternative: EJ-OVL-01 is high (15% of the allowance), EJ-MDD-02, EJ-MDD-04 and EJ-MDD-05 are medium, and the others low. Approval follows materiality: low judgements by the model owner, medium by the model owner and the head of the modelling unit, high by the MRC after review by Model Validation; the proposer is never the sole approver. Medium and high judgements were challenged by Daan Kuipers, who did not propose them, before approval, and the challenge and its resolution are recorded in the log, for example the challenge of EJ-MDD-05, which led to lowering the floor from 12.5% to 10%. The aggregate effect of all expert judgements, including the overlays, is EUR 20.1 million or 21% of the allowance, which exceeds the high materiality threshold and was approved by the MRC on 18 March 2027. Manual stage overrides are permitted only within the override policy in section 6 of the ECL operating procedure OP-ECL-04, which lists the permitted reasons in a closed list (information on imminent unemployment or divorce not yet reflected in the data, confirmed fraud investigation, and errors in input data pending correction), limits overrides to an upward transfer to Stage 2, and requires relevant information not captured by the model. Each override records the reason code, a written rationale with supporting evidence, the proposer from Collections and the approver from Credit Risk Management, independent of the proposer. Override rates, direction and magnitude are monitored quarterly by reason and approving unit; the rate was 0.4% of loan parts in 2026, below the retail analysis threshold of 5%.

sections.heading: Expert judgement in model design
sections.text: The design judgements are justified in this document: the single PD model with segment drivers instead of segment models (EJ-MDD-01, section 2.2), the two-year reversion period at the upper end of FIN-STD-200 §9.4 (EJ-MDD-02, section 4.3.2), the rejection of GDP as a driver (EJ-MDD-03, section 4.3.1), the NHG claim acceptance rate of 94% (EJ-MDD-04) and the floor of 10% on the forced-sale discount (EJ-MDD-05, section 4.4). EJ-MDD-04 uses the observed acceptance rate of 2016–2026 claims (1,212 claims) rather than the lower 2013–2015 rate, because the NHG conditions were tightened in 2014 and the Bank's claim handling was centralised in 2016. EJ-MDD-05 sets a floor because the observed discount fell to 8.1% in 2021–2022, when the housing market was exceptionally tight, which is not considered representative for the lifetime of the portfolio.

sections.heading: Overlays
sections.text: Each overlay addresses a specific identified model limitation, is quantified by a documented method and has a plan with target date to remove the limitation: OVL-M-01 addresses L-01 and is to be removed by model version 4.0, and OVL-M-02 addresses L-02 and is to be removed when the climate-adjusted collateral indexation becomes available. Both overlays are recorded in the overlay register with rationale, limitation addressed, affected portfolio and stages, quantification method, amount, approval, review date and remediation plan, and are documented in the management overlay memo EVD-07-OVL. OVL-M-01 (EUR 14.6 million at 31 December 2026) exceeds EUR 5 million and was approved by the Group Impairment Committee after review by Model Validation; OVL-M-02 (EUR 3.8 million, 4% of the portfolio allowance) was approved jointly by the Head of IFRS 9 Modelling and the Head of Finance Reporting. Overlays are reassessed quarterly, and because OVL-M-01 had been in place for four consecutive quarters by 31 March 2026, a model change assessment under MRM-STD-050 was opened (CHG-2026-0118), which led to the planned development of version 4.0.

sections.heading: Change classification of version 3.2
sections.text: The recalibration was recorded in the change log of the model inventory on 15 January 2027 (change CHG-2027-0147), before implementation, with a change memorandum describing the change and rationale, the affected components and documents, the internal classification with analysis, the quantitative impact, the required validation and the implementation plan. The change does not alter the methodology, drivers, default definition, range of application or use and introduces no new input source; its impact at 31 December 2026 is −2.3% on the modelled ECL and 1.6% of exposure changing stage, below the 5% and 10% thresholds of MRM-STD-050 §5.2(e). It is therefore classified as internally non-material; no regulatory class applies because the model does not require supervisory permission. The cumulative impact of the changes since the last full validation in 2024 (versions 3.1 and 3.2 together: −4.1% ECL) also remains below the materiality thresholds, and the change was neither split nor combined with the planned version 4.0. MRM confirmed the classification on 2 February 2027, and the new version is approved by the model owner and recorded in the inventory.

sections.heading: Purpose and summary
sections.text: This memo documents the quarterly reassessment of the management overlays on the IFRS 9 ECL for Dutch residential mortgages (model MDL-07, ECL-MORT-NL version 3.1 in production) for the reporting date 31 March 2027, as required by FIN-STD-200 §10.6 and MRM-STD-023 §6.4. At 31 March 2027 two overlays are in place: OVL-M-01 (refinancing risk of interest-only loans at maturity) of EUR 14.2 million and OVL-M-02 (foundation subsidence risk in peat areas) of EUR 3.9 million, in total EUR 18.1 million or 19% of the portfolio loss allowance of EUR 95.3 million; both are documented, quantified and approved as set out below and reported quarterly to the MRC. The memo was prepared by Lotte Verbeek (IFRS 9 Modelling), reviewed by Daan Kuipers and approved by Maarten Hoekstra (Head of IFRS 9 Modelling) and Karin de Boer (Head of Finance Reporting) on 15 April 2027, and was presented to the Group Impairment Committee on 22 April 2027.

evidence.quote: At 31 March 2027 two overlays are in place: OVL-M-01 (refinancing risk of interest-only loans at maturity) of EUR 14.2 million and OVL-M-02 (foundation subsidence risk in peat areas) of EUR 3.9 million, in total EUR 18.1 million or 19% of the portfolio loss allowance of EUR 95.3 million; both are documented, quantified and approved as set out below and reported quarterly to the MRC.

sections.heading: Overlay register
sections.text: Both overlays are recorded in the overlay register with rationale, the model limitation addressed, the affected portfolio and stages, the quantification method, the amount, the approval, the review date and the remediation plan. OVL-M-01: limitation L-01; interest-only loan parts maturing in 2027–2034 with indexed LTV above 80% or a refinancing capacity shortfall (5,410 loan parts, EUR 1.23 billion); Stage 2; alternative model run with PD uplift; EUR 14.2 million; Group Impairment Committee, first approved 19 June 2025, last renewed 22 April 2027; review 30 June 2027; remediation by model version 4.0. OVL-M-02: limitation L-02; loan parts secured by properties built before 1970 on peat soils with high foundation risk (9,800 loan parts, EUR 2.41 billion); Stages 1 and 2; collateral haircut; EUR 3.9 million; Head of IFRS 9 Modelling and Head of Finance Reporting, first approved 18 December 2025; review 30 June 2027; remediation by climate-adjusted collateral indexation.

evidence.quote: Both overlays are recorded in the overlay register with rationale, the model limitation addressed, the affected portfolio and stages, the quantification method, the amount, the approval, the review date and the remediation plan.

sections.heading: OVL-M-01 – limitation and rationale
sections.text: OVL-M-01 addresses limitation L-01: the PD model does not capture the refinancing risk of interest-only loans at their bullet maturity, because the development data contain few maturities of such loans, while the loans originated in 1997–2004 with 30-year terms mature from 2027 onwards. Households whose interest-only part matures must refinance under current lending standards, which cap interest-only borrowing at 50% of the property value, or repay from other assets; the AFM and the Bank's own customer contact programme have identified a group with insufficient repayment capacity. The out-of-time calibration of the interest-only segment (observed 0.52% against predicted 0.44%) and the observed default rate of 1.9% of interest-only loans within 24 months before maturity in 2019–2026, against a model PD of 0.6% for the same loans, provide the quantitative evidence of the limitation. The overlay is not used to smooth results: it is linked to this specific limitation and will be released when the limitation is removed.

evidence.quote: OVL-M-01 addresses limitation L-01: the PD model does not capture the refinancing risk of interest-only loans at their bullet maturity, because the development data contain few maturities of such loans, while the loans originated in 1997–2004 with 30-year terms mature from 2027 onwards.

sections.heading: OVL-M-01 – quantification
sections.text: The overlay is quantified by an alternative model run: for the affected population the marginal PDs in the 24 months around maturity are multiplied by 3.1, the ratio of the observed to the modelled default rate in the evidence window, and lifetime ECL is calculated in all three scenarios with the probability weights of the quarter. The multiplier is expert judgement EJ-OVL-01 in the expert judgement log, with its rationale, the alternatives considered (a flat PD floor and a Stage 3-like LGD) and the quantified impact of EUR 14.2 million, in accordance with MRM-STD-023. The overlay moves with the forward-looking forecasts: it is EUR 11.9 million in the upside, EUR 13.1 million in the baseline and EUR 17.8 million in the downside scenario, so that it is directionally consistent with the scenarios and serves as an interim solution until the model change. The decrease from EUR 14.6 million at 31 December 2026 results from 70 loan parts that were refinanced or repaid in the quarter and from the higher house price index.

sections.text: Because the overlay reflects a significant increase in credit risk that the staging model does not capture, the affected loan parts are transferred collectively to Stage 2, so that the stage allocation is consistent with the lifetime measurement. Loan parts leave the collective transfer when the interest-only part is refinanced, converted or repaid, or when the obligor's refinancing capacity has been confirmed in the customer contact programme.

sections.heading: OVL-M-02 – foundation subsidence
sections.text: OVL-M-02 addresses limitation L-02: the collateral indexation does not reflect the value impact of foundation damage expected for older properties on peat soils as groundwater levels fall, a physical climate risk not captured by the model. The affected population is identified from public foundation risk maps combined with the construction year and soil type recorded in the collateral system; 9,800 loan parts with EUR 2.41 billion are in the high-risk class. The overlay is quantified by applying a collateral haircut of 15%, based on published repair cost estimates and observed price discounts for properties with known foundation problems, and recalculating the LGD in all scenarios, which gives EUR 3.9 million. As the overlay is below EUR 5 million and below 5% of the portfolio loss allowance, it was approved jointly by the Head of IFRS 9 Modelling and the Head of Finance Reporting. The affected loan parts are not transferred to Stage 2, because the risk affects the loss severity and not the risk of default.

documents.title: Data quality assessment report – IFRS 9 Mortgages RDS 2026

sections.heading: Scope and approach
sections.text: This report documents the data quality assessment of the frozen reference data set RDS-ECLM-2026-v1.0 of model MDL-07, performed before the re-estimation for model version 3.2 in accordance with MRM-STD-022 §5.1. The assessment was performed by IFRS 9 Modelling (Lotte Verbeek) with the Data Stewards of the six data domains between 13 and 25 March 2027, using the data quality rules of the Group DQ monitoring tool and additional checks in the build code. As the model is Tier 1, the assessment includes sample-based verification against source documentation in addition to reconciliations and automated rules. The report covers 76.4 million loan-part-months and 21,340 default events over January 2012 – December 2026. Results are reported per rule, variable and dimension in the annex to this report; the sections below summarise them.

evidence.quote: This report documents the data quality assessment of the frozen reference data set RDS-ECLM-2026-v1.0 of model MDL-07, performed before the re-estimation for model version 3.2 in accordance with MRM-STD-022 §5.1.

sections.heading: Critical data elements and rules
sections.text: The 46 critical data elements (38 input variables and eight target constituents) have 214 data quality rules, at least one per applicable mandatory dimension, defined jointly by the model developer and the Data Stewards and documented in the RDS documentation; the reason is recorded where a dimension is not applicable, for example timeliness for the origination date. Every rule has an amber and a red threshold at least as strict as the defaults of MRM-STD-022 §4.3 (completeness amber below 98% and red below 95%, reconciliation amber above 0.5% and red above 1%, logical consistency amber below 99% and red below 98%, timeliness amber at refresh plus one month and red at refresh plus three months). No threshold less strict than the defaults is used.

Attribute-level completeness (share of non-missing values per variable) is above 99% for 41 of the 46 critical data elements; the exceptions are the original valuation (94.1%, red, DD-03), the energy label (82%, not a critical element), the watchlist status before 2019 (structurally missing, DD-04), the prepayment reason code 2012–2014 (91%, amber, DD-05) and the household income at origination for loans before 2006 (97.6%, amber). Missing household income is imputed with the median loan-to-income of the origination cohort and product, affecting 1.2% of loan parts.

Realised losses and write-offs reconcile to the finance subledger within 0.2% per year, and the RDS exposures are consistent with the data used in the FINREP non-performing exposure templates. sections.heading: Analysis of amber results and actions
sections.text: Each amber result was analysed by the model owner and its cause documented: the indexed LTV PSI reflects the house price increase, and the P07 overestimation reflects lower market rates at rate reset than assumed in the payment shock variable. As the indexed LTV PSI was amber in two consecutive quarters, it was notified to MRM and Model Validation on 20 February 2027, within ten business days of the result, and a root cause analysis with action plan was submitted on 14 March 2027. The action plan proposes no action for the LTV PSI, justified by the driver capturing a genuine risk change, and recalibration of the payment shock variable in version 4.0 for P07; model changes are processed under MRM-STD-050.

sections.heading: Annual model review 2026 – conclusion
sections.text: The annual model review covered the monitoring results, changes in the portfolio (growth of 3.1%, lower interest-only share) and environment (house price increase, stable unemployment), the open findings and data deficiencies, the expert judgement log and overlays, and the consistency between code and documentation. The model owner concludes that the model remains fit for purpose, subject to the overlays in place, that recalibration (version 3.2) is required, and that the change for interest-only refinancing risk (version 4.0) is to be developed; the review was signed off by Maarten Hoekstra on 12 March 2027 and submitted to MRM. The model owner confirmed the consistency between the production code, the implementation specification and the MDD for 2026 on the basis of the code–documentation review of February 2027. No re-validation trigger occurred in 2026: there was no unresolved red monitoring outcome, no material change in portfolio composition or intended use and no relevant regulatory change.

documents.title: Implementation and parallel run report – ECL-MORT-NL v3.2

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: This report documents the implementation testing, reconciliation, parallel run and user acceptance testing of model MDL-07 version 3.2 (recalibration) in the production ECL engine (release EE-2027.2), prepared by Finance IT and IFRS 9 Modelling and approved by the model owner on 28 May 2027. Version 3.2 will be used for the reporting date 30 June 2027 only after implementation testing, reconciliation, the parallel run and UAT have been completed and the version has been approved for use under MRM-POL-001; this report documents the first four conditions. Version 3.2 changes parameter values only (coefficients, calibration intercepts, prepayment and LGD parameters); the engine code is unchanged except for the parameter loader.

evidence.quote: Version 3.2 will be used for the reporting date 30 June 2027 only after implementation testing, reconciliation, the parallel run and UAT have been completed and the version has been approved for use under MRM-POL-001; this report documents the first four conditions.

sections.heading: Implementation specification
sections.text: The implementation specification IS-MDL07-v3.2 is consistent with the approved MDD version 3.2 and was approved by the model owner on 23 April 2027, before implementation started. It defines the production source field and lineage of every input variable, and identifies one difference between development and production data sources: the engine reads the indexed collateral value from the collateral system rather than recomputing it from the market value and index. It defines every transformation, missing-value and outlier treatment, formula, coefficient, lookup table and PD band boundary with precision and rounding conventions (double precision, no intermediate rounding, ECL rounded to cents at output), and contains 1,200 test cases with expected outputs generated with the development code.

sections.heading: Implementation testing
sections.text: Testing was performed by the Finance IT test team, independent of the author of the production code and, as required for a Tier 1 model, of the model development team. The tests covered all 1,200 specified test cases, the mapping of input data and all transformations, the handling of missing, invalid and boundary values and the outputs for every segment, stage and PD band. Test plan, cases, results and defects are documented in test report TR-EE-2027.2; the two defects found (rounding of the prepayment rate in the loader and the order of the scenario columns) affected outputs and were resolved and retested before sign-off.

sections.heading: Record-level reconciliation
sections.text: Production outputs were reconciled at record level with the development code outputs on identical input data for the full portfolio at 31 December 2026 (451,300 loan parts, all segments). All continuous outputs (12-month and lifetime PD, LGD, EAD and ECL per scenario) agree within 10^-6 absolute or 0.01% relative difference, and the stage allocation and PD band are identical for all loan parts. Before correction of the two defects, 3,114 loan parts were outside tolerance; all differences were investigated and explained, and no unexplained difference remains.

sections.heading: Comparison of development and production lineage
sections.text: The lineage of the development data (RDS build) and of the production input data was compared variable by variable, and the only difference is the source of the indexed collateral value. The effect of this difference on the model outputs was quantified by running the engine with both values: the ECL differs by EUR 0.04 million (0.05%) at 31 December 2026, and no loan part changes stage. The difference arises because the collateral system applies the index at property level with the valuation date to the day, whereas the RDS applies it at month level; the MDD and the implementation specification document the production approach.

sections.heading: Parallel run
sections.text: As version 3.2 is a new version of a Tier 1 model, a parallel run with version 3.1 was performed before use for financial reporting. It covered the full quarterly production cycle of Q1 2027 with the three monthly reference dates 31 January, 28 February and 31 March 2027. At 31 March 2027 the modelled ECL of version 3.2 is EUR 75.4 million against EUR 77.2 million for version 3.1 (−2.3%), 1.6% of the exposure changes stage (1.1% from Stage 2 to Stage 1, 0.5% from Stage 1 to Stage 2), the average 12-month PD decreases from 0.45% to 0.43%, and no operational issues occurred besides the two defects of section 4.

deficiencies.rationale: Section 4.6.1 states the Q4 2026 weights (50/20/30) and refers to the GDP distribution of the stochastic simulation, but the quantitative derivation of the weights (percentile bands per scenario) is not documented, and the 'Committee's view on downside risks' used to move from the simulated 55/20/25 split to 50/20/30 is not quantified.

mitigation.text: Document the quarterly derivation of the scenario weights from the simulated GDP distribution, including the judgemental adjustment and its approval by the Group Impairment Committee, in MDD section 4.6.1 and the quarterly scenario memo.

deficiencies.rationale: The PD multiplier of 3.1 for overlay OVL-M-01 (EJ-OVL-01, high materiality) is not tested by sensitivity analysis under reasonable alternative judgements; MDD section 7.6 covers EJ-MDD-02, -04 and -05 only, while the overlay is the largest expert judgement in the model.

mitigation.text: Add a sensitivity analysis of OVL-M-01 to the multiplier (for example 2.0–4.0) and to the length of the maturity window to the Q2 2027 overlay memo.

deficiencies.rationale: Limitation L-06 (single national unemployment driver) is assessed as medium without quantification and is not recorded in the model inventory, whereas MRM-STD-020 §7.3 requires material limitations to be recorded there and reported at G3.

mitigation.text: Quantify L-06 (for example with a regional unemployment variant of the PD model) and record it in the inventory limitations field.

deficiencies.rationale: The threshold calibration in MDD section 4.2.3 is documented with the capture-rate and volatility trade-off, but Model Validation's out-of-time recomputation per origination vintage shows that the capture rate of the selected thresholds falls to 54% for loans originated in 2022–2024, whose origination PDs reflect the post-2022 rate environment; the calibration on 2019–2025 in aggregate masks this.

mitigation.text: Recalibrate the SICR thresholds with a vintage-level capture-rate analysis before the Q4 2027 reporting date, and assess an interim collective Stage 2 transfer for 2022–2024 originations.

deficiencies.rationale: MDD section 4.4 states that the LGD is a best estimate without downturn adjustment, but Model Validation's analysis shows that the forced-sale discount of 12.5% is driven by the 2016–2018 sales, which still included auction sales from the 2012–2014 downturn workouts; on 2019–2026 sales only the discount is 10.4%, so the parameter contains an implicit downturn component (ECL impact about −EUR 2.6 million).

mitigation.text: Re-estimate the forced-sale discount on a sample representative of current market conditions, or document why the 2016–2018 sales are representative, and quantify the effect on ECL.
